h1: Crans-Montana ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Crans-Montana sits on a terrace at 1,547 metres above the Rhone valley, and its ski area runs from the Plaine Morte Glacier at 3,000 metres down to the golf course on the Haut-Plateau at 1,500. The operator describes all 140 kilometres of marked pistes as completely south-facing - the whole mountain turned towards the sun and the Valais Alps opposite.
stayOverview: Crans and Montana are two halves of the same terrace, joined along one road: Crans is the shopping end, Montana has the funicular up from Sierre in the valley below.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Either half puts you on the terrace with the same view south over the Rhone valley.
rentalCars: Crans-Montana is reached by the funicular from Sierre or by the road up from the Rhone valley.

lifts.unannounced: No lift count is published on the operator’s ski or winter-season pages.

verticalDrop.unannounced: The operator states an altitude range of 1,500 to 3,000 m but publishes no vertical drop; subtracting the two would be our arithmetic.

season.unannounced: No season dates are published on the operator’s ski page or its winter-season page.

snowpark.note: The operator places it on the descent from the Plaine Morte Glacier to the Haut-Plateau but gives it no name of its own.

baseElevation.note: The operator states an altitude ranging from 1,500 to 3,000 m - 4,920 to 9,840 feet.

longestRun.unannounced: The operator publishes the altitude range and 140 km of south-facing marked pistes, but names no longest run.

dayPass.unannounced: The lift company's winter rates page publishes only its season passes - Pass One and its variants - and sends day-ticket buyers to its webshop, where the price depends on the date. Its own skiing pages carry no day rate either.
